wiki.briefHistory: The Alabama State Hornets are the college football team representing Alabama State University. The Hornets play in NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision (FCS) as a member of the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC). Hornet Stadium serves as the facility for Alabama State football games and practices. The 120-yard field turf playing field provides training to ASU football in all weather conditions. In June 2011, construction on the Houston Markham Football Complex was completed. The two-story, 30,000-square-foot facility serves as the new home of the football program.

wiki.briefHistory: Delaware State University was established on May 15, 1891, by the Delaware General Assembly as the Delaware College for Colored Students under the Morrill Act of 1890. One of the nation's earliest land-grant HBCUs, DSU was founded on a 95-acre property north of Dover with an initial $8,000 state appropriation. After several name changes - including State College for Colored Students and Delaware State College - it achieved university status in 1993. DSU made history in 2021 by becoming the first HBCU to acquire a non-HBCU institution, Wesley College. Today it enrolls over 6,000 students across its 356-acre campus and is widely recognized as one of the nation's premier HBCUs.

wiki.briefHistory: Howard University was founded on March 2, 1867, by Civil War General Oliver O. Howard, just two years after the end of the Civil War. Chartered by an Act of Congress, it is one of the nation's most storied HBCUs and the only one classified as a Carnegie Research University with very high research activity. Over its 158-year history, Howard has trained generations of Black leaders across law, medicine, business, and the arts - including Thurgood Marshall, Kamala Harris, and Chadwick Boseman. Home to 14 schools and colleges and approximately 14,900 students, Howard is consistently ranked the #1 HBCU in the nation by Forbes and is the founding site of five of the nine NPHC organizations.

wiki.briefHistory: Morgan State University was founded in 1867 as the Centenary Biblical Institute by the Methodist Episcopal Church in Baltimore, Maryland. Originally created to train Black men for the ministry, it evolved into a liberal arts institution and was renamed Morgan College in 1890 in honor of early benefactor Reverend Lyttleton Morgan. After transferring from the Methodist Church to the State of Maryland in 1939, it expanded significantly and was redesignated Morgan State University in 1975. Today Maryland's largest HBCU, Morgan enrolls over 10,700 students and holds Carnegie Doctoral University status, with a mission to serve as Maryland's Preeminent Public Urban Research University.

wiki.briefHistory: North Carolina Central University was founded in 1909 by Dr. James E. Shepard, a pharmacist and visionary educator, who opened the National Religious Training School and Chautauqua in Durham, NC, supported by private funds from both Northern and Southern philanthropists. It became a state institution in 1923 and joined the University of North Carolina system in 1972. NCCU is the nation's first public liberal arts HBCU and has grown into a comprehensive research university offering programs through law, library science, business, and STEM disciplines. The Eagles have produced notable alumni across law, politics, and entertainment, and the football program captured the HBCU National Championship in 2022 and 2023.

wiki.briefHistory: Norfolk State University was founded in 1935 as the Norfolk Unit of Virginia Union University, initially serving 85 students. It became an independent institution in 1942, joined Virginia State College by legislative act, and was renamed Norfolk State College in 1969 when it gained full accreditation with an enrollment of 5,400. It achieved university status in 1979. NSU is a comprehensive urban HBCU located in Norfolk, Virginia, offering programs through eight schools and colleges. The Spartans are celebrated for their basketball program's 2012 NCAA Tournament upset of #2 Missouri as a 15-seed, one of the greatest upsets in tournament history. NSU owns one of the largest on-campus FCS football stadiums in the country.

The color combination was adopted as the university grew from a small commuter college into a nationally recognized HBCU.

wiki.briefHistory: South Carolina State University traces its roots to 1872, when the South Carolina Agricultural and Mechanical Institute was established within Claflin College under the Morrill Land Grant Act. In 1896, the South Carolina General Assembly created a fully separate institution - the Colored Normal Industrial Agricultural and Mechanical College of South Carolina - in Orangeburg. Renamed South Carolina State College in 1954 and elevated to university status in 1992, SCSU is the only public HBCU land-grant research institution in South Carolina. The Bulldogs are one of MEAC's most successful football programs, having won 19 MEAC championships and seven HBCU national titles (including the most recent in 2025), and produced Pro Football Hall of Famers Deacon Jones, Marion Motley, Harry Carson, and Donnie Shell.

wiki.colorsDescription: Garnet and Navy Blue. Garnet - a rich, deep red - is a color shared across the state of South Carolina as a symbol of pride and resilience, connecting SC State to its role as the state's flagship HBCU and land-grant institution. Navy blue represents steadfastness, dignity, and the depth of tradition built over more than 125 years. Together, the colors speak to SC State's identity as both a South Carolina institution and a national powerhouse in HBCU athletics and academics.
